title: Really Good Kedgeree
subtitle: Smoked haddock, curried rice & soft-boiled eggs · under an hour
description: Smoked haddock poached with bay, basmati cooked in the fish liquor, then folded through buttery curried onions with peas, cream, parsley and lemon, and topped with quartered boiled eggs.

ingredients.note: rinsed in cold water and drained

steps.text: Lay the {{haddock}} skin-side up in a large frying pan. Add the {{water}} and {{bay}}, then bring to a gentle simmer.
Poach until the fish is just cooked and flakes easily. Drain through a colander set over a bowl so you keep the cooking liquid, and throw away the bay leaves.
Tip the reserved liquid into a saucepan, stir in the {{rice}}, cover and bring to the boil. Turn the heat right down and simmer very gently.
Turn the heat off and leave the rice covered until it has soaked up all the liquid.
Meanwhile, lower the {{eggs}} into a small pan of boiling water. Drain, cool under cold running water, then peel and set aside.
If using, cook the {{peas}} in a little boiling water and drain.
Melt the {{butter}} with the {{oil}} in a large frying pan. Add the {{onion}} and cook over a low heat, stirring now and then, until well softened.
Add the {{curry}} and cook, stirring constantly.
Stir the cooked rice into the onions, then add the peas, {{cream}}, {{parsley}} and a few twists of {{pepper}}.
Break the haddock into chunky flakes and add to the pan. Gently stir in the juice of the {{lemon}} and heat through.
Quarter the eggs and arrange them on top. Cover with a lid until the eggs are warm, then serve.

notes: Not serving straight away? Tip it into a warm dish, dot with a few cubes of butter, cover with foil and keep warm in a low oven for up to 20 minutes.
Hot-smoked salmon version: skip poaching the fish and cook the rice in 500ml light chicken stock instead. Flake the salmon in with the peas.
Check the curry powder label if you need it to be strictly gluten-free.

nutrition.note: Rough estimate from the ingredients (with peas); smoked haddock salt varies a lot by brand.
